title: Egg-yolk tile watched by a camera in a domestic dishwasher (55 C, pH 10.5, protease 0.06 g/L)

provenance.source: R. Perez-Mohedano, PhD thesis, University of Birmingham, chapter 7, Tables 7.1 to 7.3 (docs/research/soils.md section 6.1)

sri.description: stain removal index from the CIELAB b* of a CFT DM-22 egg-yolk tile, imaged on line through the main wash; triplicates

provenance.notes: A weak observation. The original was a Whirlpool DU750 held at 55 C with a model detergent; here it is laid on the owner's Bosch on Eco 50 with the main wash heated to 55 C, the tile standing in the lower basket facing the middle. Times are counted from the release of the detergent (1050 s into Eco 50). The removed share is read as (time - 5 min lag) x 1.75 %/min in the constant-rate stage, complete at about 65 min; the residual mass fraction is one minus that. The stated uncertainties cover the scatter of the triplicates (0.29 %/min) and the difference of machine, temperature course and detergent.

detergent.product: model detergent with 0.06 g/L protease granulate at pH 10.5

soils.recipe: CFT DM-22: egg yolk on melamine, 1.75 g on 120 x 100 mm, aged

drying.conditions: as supplied by the tile maker
